properties.areaDesc: Coconino, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 1:56AM MST until October 22 at 2:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected along
Moenkopi Wash and the Little Colorado River.

* WHERE...Moenkopi Wash and the Little Colorado River from Cameron to
the Colorado River confluence.

* WHEN...Until 200 PM MST /300 PM MDT/ Tonight.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of Moenkopi Wash and the Little Colorado River
is occurring. Further rises in the water levels of already flooded
creeks and normally dry washes. Deadly flooding over low-water
crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 152 AM MST /252 AM MDT/, Water levels in Moenkopi Wash
remained above major flood stage. Elevated flow was also observed
on the Little Colorado River near Cameron. With additional heavy
rain expected, flooding is expected to continue.
- This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Hamblin Wash, Begashibito Wash, Little Colorado River, Moenkopi
Wash, Bekihatso Wash, Fivemile Wash and Sheep Wash.

Flooding is occurring along Moenkopi Wash.
- For Moenkopi Wash near Tuba City:
At 12:45am MST /1:45am MDT/ the stage was 33.55 feet.
Flood Stage is 27.0 feet.
Impacts:
At 27.0 feet: At 27.0 feet water begins to encroach on homes in
lower Moenkopi Village and floods crop fields along the river.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Tuba City, Moenkopi, Little Colorado River Navajo Tribal Park and
Salt Trail Canyon.
- This includes the following recreation areas andcampgrounds...
Blue Water Base Camp and Old Fish Camp Site.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 22 at 2:45AM MDT until October 23 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Castle
Country, Central Mountains, San Rafael Swell, Bryce Canyon Country,
Capitol Reef National Park and Vicinity, Glen Canyon Recreation
Area/Lake Powell, South Central Utah, Southern Mountains, Upper
Sevier River Valleys, Western Canyonlands, Lower Washington County
and Zion National Park.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A late season surge of tropical moisture will bring widespread
moderate to at times heavy rainfall across much of southern Utah
through Thursday. Local rainfall totals in excess of 3 inches are
expected through Thursday evening.
- All normally dry washes, small streams and mainstem rivers will
see elevated flows from this excessive rainfall, with periods of
heavier rainfall resulting in flash flooding. Backcountry roads
may become impassable due to flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

People in the backcountry should ensure they have alternative routes
available in case their primary route becomes impassable.

properties.areaDesc: Upper Columbia Basin; Okanogan Valley; Waterville Plateau
properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 22 at 1:10AM PDT until October 23 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS Spokane WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Northwest winds 15 to 30 mph with gusts up to 50 mph
expected.

* WHERE...Harrington, Bridgeport, Waterville, Okanogan, Nespelem,
Grand Coulee, Disautel Pass, Coulee City, Oroville, Mansfield,
Brewster, Tonasket, Badger Mountain Road, Wilbur, Ritzville, Omak,
Odessa, and Creston.

* WHEN...From midnight tonight to 3 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.
Motorists traveling along Highway 2 between Creston and Douglas
should take extra precaution and be prepared for strong cross
winds. Patchy blowing dust will be possible. New fire starts could
spread swiftly through dry fuel beds, especially in the afternoon
as humidity values lower near 20 percent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds will increase after midnight with peak
gusts between 3AM and 11AM. The axis of strongest winds will be
through the Okanogan Valley, across northwestern Douglas County and
into northern Grant and western Lincoln County between Creston and
Coulee City.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

NWSheadline: WIND ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM MIDNIGHT TONIGHT TO 3 PM PDT FRIDAY

expected.

* WHERE...Sherman Pass, Highway 20 Wauconda Summit, Inchelium,

* WHEN...From midnight tonight to 3 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.
Isolated to scattered tree damage will be possible in the
mountains.  New fire starts could spread swiftly through dry fuel
beds, especially in the afternoon as humidity values lower near 25
percent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Strong winds will develop over the higher
terrain around midnight into early Friday morning. Peak wind gusts
will develop between 3AM and 11AM.  Lower valleys may experience
lighter winds until Friday morning closer to 8AM.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

possible.

* WHERE...Aleutians East Borough.

* WHEN...From 10 PM Thursday to 10 PM AKDT Friday.

properties.description:
* WHAT...South to southeast winds 35 to 50 mph with gusts up to 75
mph.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta, Western Capes, and Northern Bristol Bay
Coast.

* WHEN...From 7 AM Friday to 4 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High winds could move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The strongest winds are expected to start by 1
PM AKDT Friday for the Kuskokwim Delta, Northern Bristol Bay,
Platinum, and Goodnews Bay. For the Western Capes, the strongest
winds are expected near Cape Newenham, with winds for Platinum and
Goodnews Bay expected to be near 60 mph. For Northern Bristol Bay,
the strongest winds are expected near Togiak, while gusts up to 50
mph are expected for Dillingham. Winds are expected to steadily
diminish through Saturday as the front moves inland and weakens.
properties.instruction:
People are urged to secure loose objects that could be blown around
or damaged by the wind. Prepare for the possibility of widespread
power outages. Use caution if you must travel.
